title: Playing piano in a Detroit good-time house
summary: After her mother died she played piano for room and board at a Detroit house run by a woman from Houston, before she went to Chicago.

story.theme_name: First paying gigs: getting started as a young professional
story.community_name: First paid gigs: pay, bands and young beginnings

blocks.x: Yeah, see, I got more off of (unintelligible). When I first come to Detroit, I never could see no daytime here. Everytime I'd go to bed, it would be night, I would wake up, it would be night. So I used to (unintelligible) girl I was staying with, you know, I said, "(Inaudible). Do the sun ever shine here? I go to bed and it's night, you know, I wake up and it's night." I said, "Do the sun ever shine here?" (Unintelligible) and I played the piano (inaudible) and I'd wake up, it would be dark again, you know.
Where were you playing the piano then?
At (unintelligible), you know, and I just played the piano there.
Well, I thought they only had men playing
pianos in the good time houses.
Anybody they could get to play piano.
Uh-huh. That's when you first came to Detroit?

Yeah, uh-huh. And I played -- the girl I played for, she came from Houston, too. And she got a house in Detroit and she knew me, knew I could play, and (unintelligible) give me a room. She give me room and board. And I (unintelligible). I didn't have a dime. I just got room and board (unintelligible) her daughter or her sister or something.
Were you married at that time?
Yeah, I was married. But my husband didn't
Uh-huh.
Yeah, (unintelligible).
When was that? Do you remember what year that was when you played the piano at the good time house?
Mama died in '23.
Uh-huh.
That was before you went to Chicago?
Oh, yeah, because after Mama died -- see, my brother Buddy was staying in Chicago. And --
Uh-huh. But you played the piano in --
I was playing the piano all the time
everywhere then.
But you played it in that place, in the good time house. That was before you --
No, I played piano period, you know.
Yes, I know that.

And then when Mama died and I went to Chicago, well, my husband ________ told me that he was getting her, and his brother was kind of fooling around with Jerry Lee (PHONETIC) and that's the girl I ________ -- she was much older than I was, you know -- and he say (unintelligible), say, " ________ get old Mack to come here. (Unintelligible) said, "Sippie can play music for us," you know. So (unintelligible).
Well, did anybody try to hit on you while you were playing the piano?
Yeah. I had plenty of boys. But (unintelligible) doing all right. I played the piano (unintelligible). Then sometimes they just give me some money, you know, (inaudible). (Unintelligible).
That's before you recorded.
Oh, yeah.
And do you remember some of the tunes you used to play? And did you sing, too?
(Unintelligible) was one of them, you know.
